title: Formal AI: deliver verified-release persistence and serving-backend provenance in one PR
body:
## Goal

Deliver the two Hive Mind fixes for the Formal AI subsystem together in **one pull request**: preserve the verified release across task acquisition, and prove which backend actually serves each task.

## Sub-issues

- [ ] #2207 — Preserve the accepted, verified Formal AI image/digest after idle update and use it for subsequent tasks instead of reverting to the bootstrap image.
- [ ] #2208 — Separate local wrapper version from serving backend provenance, probe and validate the actual endpoint, and record the serving version and managed image digest in task evidence.

The sub-issues contain exact source locations, executed failing reproductions, and detailed regression requirements. Preserve those requirements; this parent coordinates their delivery rather than replacing their evidence.

## Single-PR delivery contract

- Implement **both sub-issues in a single Hive Mind pull request**, referencing this parent and including `Fixes #2207` and `Fixes #2208` in its description.
- Turn both supplied reproductions into automated regressions and cover the interaction: successful verified update → stopped sidecar → next task acquisition → actual backend health/version/digest → release → subsequent acquisition, including persisted-state restart.
- Preserve explicit operator pins, active leases, memory compatibility and rollback guarantees; identify the accepted immutable image rather than trusting a mutable tag.
- Cover wrapper/backend version mismatch, unsupported or unavailable backends, malformed health responses, authentication, and stale cached provenance. Do not infer the server version from a local executable.
- Supply test output and real published-image evidence demonstrating that the accepted release is the backend used by the next task. A successful updater status or local `--version` alone is insufficient.
- Replay the referenced real-client tasks and verify issue reading, requested source/workflow changes, tests, commit, push, and the actual remote PR diff. If an independently tracked Formal AI defect still prevents delivery, report that blocker explicitly; do not claim end-to-end success from a plan-only response or an empty PR.

## Responsibility boundary

Both sub-issues are Hive Mind lifecycle/provenance responsibilities. The separate tool resource-scope and argument-grounding defect is tracked in [Formal AI #1075](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1075); it is related context, **not a third sub-issue or a request to fold Formal AI source changes into this Hive Mind PR**.

The published release is real, but the failed task logs do not establish the exact serving version or prove the reproduced update/acquire transition occurred on that host. The combined fix must remove that ambiguity and prevent the independently reproduced lifecycle failure.
